D: An inventor and his dog run a humane pest control business just before the town's giant vegetable competition.
P: Serve the cheese when Wallace gets the crackers out.
S: Wallace and his love of cheese
Wensleydale with cranberries, a crumbly Lancashire or aged cheddar and a soft blue, with water crackers, apple slices and a pot of chutney.
Prize veg bubble and squeak cakes

Mashed potato, cabbage, carrot and leek pan-fried into crisp golden cakes with melted cheddar, served with brown sauce and a dollop of chutney. Boil 800g potatoes and mash with 30g butter. Shred a quarter savoy cabbage and 1 leek, grate 1 carrot and fry in butter for 6 minutes until soft. Mix into the mash with 80g grated cheddar, salt and pepper. Shape into 12 small cakes and chill 20 minutes. Fry in butter and oil over medium heat for 4 minutes a side until deep golden. Serve with brown sauce and chutney.
the van with the bunnies in the back
Shortcrust filled with grated cheddar, potato and onion, crimped, egg washed, baked at 200C for 25 minutes until golden.
M: Gromit's prize marrow, finally on a plate
Zucchini or marrow halved, filled with lamb mince cooked with onion, tomato and herbs, covered in cheese and baked at 190C for 35 minutes.
Tottington Hall roast beef and Yorkshires

Rare roast sirloin with tall Yorkshire puddings, crisp roast potatoes, honey carrots and rich beef gravy, horseradish on the side. Heat the oven to 220C. Rub a 1.2kg beef sirloin with oil, salt and pepper and roast 15 minutes, then at 180C for 25 to 30 minutes to 52C inside. Rest 20 minutes. Roast 1kg parboiled potatoes in hot oil for 45 minutes. Whisk 3 eggs, 150ml milk and 120g plain flour, pour into a very hot oiled 12-hole tin and bake 20 minutes at 220C. Roast 500g carrots with honey. Make gravy with the pan juices, flour and 400ml beef stock.
W: Grated carrot, walnuts, oil, brown sugar, eggs and spice mixed with self-raising flour, baked at 170C for 50 minutes, cream cheese frosting on top.
K: the kettle at 62 West Wallaby Street

Earl Grey tea brewed strong and chilled, mixed with fresh lemon syrup and topped with sparkling water over ice, lemon wheels and mint in the jug. Steep 4 Earl Grey tea bags in 800ml boiling water for 4 minutes, remove and cool. Simmer 100g caster sugar with 100ml water and the peeled zest of 2 lemons for 3 minutes, then cool and strain. Stir the syrup and the juice of 3 lemons into the tea. Pour over ice and top with 400ml sparkling water, with lemon wheels and mint.

s.note: Wallace and his love of cheese
s.how: Take 150g Wensleydale, 150g aged cheddar and 100g blue cheese out of the fridge an hour ahead. Arrange with water crackers, apple slices and a pot of apple chutney. Not a lot of people know that.

s.note: the van with the bunnies in the back
s.how: Mix 200g grated cheddar with a finely diced potato and onion. Cut 3 sheets shortcrust into rounds, fill, fold and crimp. Egg wash and bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden.

m.note: Gromit's prize marrow, finally on a plate
m.how: Halve 4 large zucchini and scoop out the middles. Fry 500g lamb mince with an onion, a tin of tomatoes and thyme for 15 minutes. Fill the zucchini, cover with 150g grated cheddar and bake at 190C for 35 minutes.

w.how: Mix 300g grated carrot, 100g walnuts, 200ml oil, 200g brown sugar, 3 eggs and spice. Fold in 250g self-raising flour and bake at 170C for 50 minutes. Frost with 250g cream cheese beaten with 200g icing sugar. Rabbit-proof the kitchen.
